study_identification.title: Normative modelling of molecular-based functional circuits captures clinical heterogeneity transdiagnostically in psychiatric patients

study_characteristics.study_objective: Combine REACT with normative modelling to build molecular-enriched functional connectivity (FC) networks and quantify individual-level deviations in schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and ADHD, linking deviations to transdiagnostic symptom dimensions.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: ROI-wise 1×4 ANOVAs with permutation testing in FSL PALM (2,000 perms; FDR); lower-level t-contrasts; summary mean deviation metrics with 1×4 ANOVA (Tukey); binary logistic regression with ROC/AUC; within/between-group similarity via correlation matrices and KS/Friedman/Conover tests; mass-univariate deviation–symptom regressions (PALM).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Normative models of molecular-enriched FC revealed significant deviations in SCHZ and BPD (not ADHD), and deviations mapped to transdiagnostic symptom dimensions, linking molecular-enriched networks to shared psychopathology across diagnoses.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Models trained on 70% HCs (CamCAN+UCLA) and tested on 30% showed moderate EV, varying by system and ROI; only ROIs with positive EV were analysed (of 443 total, NAT 319; DAT 307; SERT 296; VAChT 257; mGluR5 418; GABA-A 421). Group comparisons of deviation scores identified significant effects in VAChT (HCUCLA vs SCHZ) and mGluR5 (HCUCLA vs SCHZ and BPD), with spatially localised clusters. Transdiagnostically, PCA of 28 symptom measures yielded components including PC2 (psychotic/depressive/inattentive/impulsive). Deviation–symptom relationships were significant for VAChT and mGluR5 (negative associations with PC2), indicating lower-than-normative FC relates to greater symptom severity across diagnoses.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Use of group-average PET/SPECT templates acquired in separate cohorts with differing resolutions; moderate collinearity among some molecular systems; cross-sectional design; relatively small clinical cohorts; deviation–symptom mapping tested in a single dataset; potential treatment effects in clinical groups.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Transdiagnostic symptom PCA combined with normative deviation mapping suggests a shared molecular–functional substrate; simple mean deviation summaries showed some classification utility; pipeline demonstrates integrating REACT with site-aware HBR normative models.

general_notes.general_notes: Population-based molecular templates: NAT (n=10; [11C]O-methylreboxetine), DAT (n=30; 123I-ioflupane SPECT), SERT (n=16; [11C]DASB), VAChT (n=6; [18F]-FEOBV), GABA-A (n=6; [11C]flumazenil-based), mGluR5 (n=31; [(11)C]ABP688); all resampled to 2 mm and normalised (0–1). Parcellation combined cortical (Schaefer), subcortical (Desikan), and cerebellar (Diedrichsen) atlases.
